title: Fat controller
tagline: The controller ends up knowing about Stripe, email, inventory, and your birthday.
history: A classic Rails smell: the framework makes controller code so easy to write that business logic quietly piles up there.
useCases: The controller talks to payment / mail / external services directly
Logic you can't test without a full request
The same flow copy-pasted across actions
whenToUse: Extract a service object (a PORO) named after the business verb — PlaceOrder, not OrderService. Now it's testable without a request.
whenNotToUse: A three-line action doesn't need a service. Rails is fine, actually.
complexity: Refactor target: move the story into an object with a single call.

codeContrast.good:
# app/controllers/orders_controller.rb
class OrdersController < ApplicationController
  def create
    result = PlaceOrder.call(order_params,
                             coupon: params[:coupon],
                             token:  params[:token])
    redirect_to result.order
  end
end

# app/services/place_order.rb — named after the business verb
class PlaceOrder
  def self.call(...) = new(...).call

  def initialize(attrs, coupon:, token:)
    @attrs, @coupon, @token = attrs, coupon, token
  end

  def call
    # Stripe, mailer, inventory, totals — all here, all
    # testable without a request. Returns a small result object.
  end
end
